sections.heading: Use the CLI in development and CI
sections.text: Run report when reviewing a new integration or before merging, and archive the stdout diagnostic alongside human review. report has no --json, --strict or --fail-on-findings option. A completed report exits 0 even with missing/invalid snapshot evidence, skipped files or warnings; even an unreadable scan directory can yield a successful report with skipped files. Usage errors and uncaught failures exit 1. Do not use exit 0 as a CI protection or completeness gate. There is no reliable report findings-failure contract to demonstrate in GitHub Actions. rotation-readiness has its own explicit JSON and verifiability gate below; those flags do not apply to report.

sections.heading: Reporting versus simulation, scan and codegen
sections.text: Choose by the evidence you have and the side effects you intend. None of these operations proves production write integrity or deployed repair.

sections.heading: CLI command reference
sections.text: Commands below describe the selected SDK version. The prepared release notice at the top of this page applies: the additional source-fix commands belong to the prepared Node release and are absent from the last published alpha.2 CLI. Arguments shown are required unless bracketed. No universal --help/--version or output-format flag is implemented. Invalid invocation exits 1; diagnostics go to stderr. report may also print a brand banner before its text.

sections.heading: report command
sections.text: Syntax: agindow report <directory> [--snapshot <local-file.json>]. Example: npx --no-install agindow report . --snapshot ./evidence.json. Prints inventory/evidence text; exit 0 after reporting, including invalid snapshot warnings. Read-only except caller shell redirection. Snapshot schema is {version: 1, window: {start, end}, events: [...], recordings?: [...]}; ISO timestamps must be ordered and include all events. Events use the frozen drift-event schema and unique IDs. A recording supplies tool, contract, args and recorded; contract.tool must match tool. Limits: snapshot 1 MiB, 10000 events, 256 recordings. Invalid snapshots produce “Invalid registry snapshot; drift evidence unavailable.” and do not fail the command.

sections.heading: codegen command
sections.text: Syntax: agindow codegen <local-contracts.json>. Example: npx --no-install agindow codegen ./contracts.json > generated.ts. Emits sandbox evaluator TypeScript to stdout; the shell writes generated.ts. Input is {version: 1, contracts: [...]}, at most 1 MiB / 256 contracts, one contract per file. Each bounded contract specifies version: 1, id, file, tool, endpoint, method, mode and operation, with optional request/response field rules and disabled. File must be a relative actions/*.ts or syncs/*.ts path. Supported methods: get, post, put, patch, delete, request. Each encoded contract is at most 2048 bytes; each request/response has at most 64 field definitions. Field types are string, number, boolean or null, with optional required and string enum (up to 64 values). Request-only renames supply from, to, identity and confidence; up to 32 reviewed sibling rules. AGINDOW_DISABLED=true forces disabled generation; no runtime refresh is provisioned. Exit 0 on emission, 1 on invalid input/usage. Generated output is not evidence that your deployed integration was exercised.

sections.heading: scan command
sections.text: Syntax: agindow scan <directory> --snapshot <local-contracts.json>. Example: npx --no-install agindow scan . --snapshot ./contracts.json. Uses the codegen bundle schema above, not the report snapshot schema. Potentially mutating: reads and replaces supported Nango source files with generated guards through temporary files and rename. Prints Changed files and Skipped files. Exit 0 when skipped is zero; exit 1 for skipped/unsupported files, invalid usage or failure. Earlier files may already be changed when a later file is skipped. Review all diffs; failure is not rollback. Symlink/escaping/oversized paths and changed source are refused. No general-purpose project rewrite or automatic repair discovery.

sections.heading: rotation-readiness command
sections.text: Syntax: agindow rotation-readiness <events.ndjson> <facts.ndjson> --as-of <UTC> [--json] [--require=verifiable]. Example: npx --no-install agindow rotation-readiness ./events.ndjson ./facts.ndjson --as-of 2026-10-29T12:00:00Z --json --require=verifiable. Reads local event and capability-fact streams, prints a table or agindow.rotation-readiness/1 JSON. It does not rotate credentials or contact providers. Facts must use the typed tenant/connection/provider/capability evidence format, not arbitrary settings. Exit 0 after valid reporting; --require=verifiable exits 1 for an empty report or any row other than verifiable. Invalid inputs/flags exit 1. Evidence expires according to the report clock; it does not establish durable replay.

sections.heading: Local source-fix export
sections.text: These prepared-release commands read local requests and explicitly admitted committed JS/TS source. Inventory hints do not authorize edits. Exports remain unvalidated until an independent runner verifies the exact candidate. They emit JSON to stdout, do not apply a patch or open a pull request. Scope, source digests, separate generation consent and independently reviewed migration evidence are required. Keep artifacts private to the authorized repository; validate the exact candidate independently before considering publication.

rows: Local request {grant, selection}; bound manifest JSON, exit 0 when bound; abstention exit 1. Request cap 1 MiB.
Local request {grant, manifest}; re-resolves against committed source. Bound JSON exit 0; stale/unsafe/unsupported abstention exit 1.
Admitted single-token rename artifact JSON; refusal exit 1, otherwise 0. Local JSON request cap 64 KiB; explicit UTC evaluation clock.
Evidence-backed local artifact JSON; refusal exit 1, otherwise 0. Request cap 64 KiB; local references resolved relative to request, each up to 32 KiB.

sections.heading: Limitations and troubleshooting
sections.text:
Missing binary: install the selected Node package in your current project; npx --no-install intentionally refuses downloading a missing CLI. Unexpected empty inventory: the scanner recognizes static tool definitions, imported LangChain tool factories, supported Nango builders and known vendor references, not every HTTP call or arbitrary application structure. Python files are not scanned. Readable JS/TS extensions include .js, .jsx, .ts, .tsx and c/m variants; dependency/build directories are excluded. Scan bounds are 10000 files, 1 MiB per file and depth 64; symlinks are skipped.
Missing evidence: report without a snapshot cannot establish runtime drift; fix invalid windows, duplicate IDs or malformed recordings. Unexpected stdout: the brand banner and warning lines are text, not JSON. Generation failure: check supported Nango forms and local contracts, then inspect diffs before retrying scan. A report is not write-integrity proof. Missing evidence remains unavailable, not clean; offline reports do not establish production calibration, streaming coverage, durable replay or hosted readiness.

sections.heading: Types and conventions
sections.text: This reference describes the paired Node package selected above. Generic F is a Callable; T is the input object type. SDK means ReturnType<typeof createAgindow>, not an additional exported class. Runtime imports come from agindow; use import type for interfaces. The practical guide introduces the call flow before these signatures.

sections.heading: Create and initialize
sections.text:
Signature: `createAgindow(options?: Options, load?: EngineLoader): SDK`

Parameters: options supplies initial configuration, selection, work, selectiveRepair or audit. load is an advanced engine-loader seam; ordinary integrations use the default bundled engine.

Returns: An independent instance. sdk.ready is Promise<void>, resolving after the load attempt. The exported agindow singleton is created with default options.

Failures: Invalid deterministic setup throws AgindowSetupError. Engine loading failure is contained; subsequent calls emit bypass. Promise settlement does not guarantee loading succeeded or detection is configured.

Usage: `const sdk = createAgindow({ mode: 'observe' }); await sdk.ready;`

sections.heading: Guard a callable
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.guard<F extends Callable>(fn: F, options?: GuardOptions): F`

Parameters: fn is your original function. options supplies tool, operation (read by default), toolName, inputShape and call policy. Explicitly label writes/unknown operations.

Returns: The original callable type, argument and receiver behavior; synchronous remains synchronous and a Promise result remains asynchronous. Observe returns the original result by reference.

Failures: Setup misuse throws AgindowSetupError. Original exceptions propagate; policy can throw AgindowDriftError. Internal faults bypass. A response halt can follow upstream completion.

Usage: `const read = sdk.guard(() => client.orders.get(id), { tool: 'orders.get', operation: 'read' });`

sections.heading: Choose a boundary automatically
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.wrap<T extends object>(target: T, options?: ClientOptions): T`

Parameters: target may be a callable, supported tool map/array, client or HTTP target. Use an explicit adapter if more than one shape matches.

Returns: A wrapped target of type T. Unknown or unsupported targets can remain unchanged with a warning; that is not proof of inspection.

Failures: Ambiguity and deterministic misuse can throw AgindowSetupError. Per-call errors follow guard semantics.

Usage: `const guarded = sdk.wrap(readOrder, { tool: 'orders.get' });`

sections.heading: Adapt tools
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.toolAdapter<T extends object>(target: T, options?: GuardOptions): T`

Parameters: A supported ToolMap/ToolArray or executor shape. Names and operation labels come from supported entries or explicit options.

Returns: A wrapped target preserving supported executor metadata and receivers.

Failures: Unsupported/immutable executors may remain unchanged with warnings. A class requires its supported framework executor hook; response formatting repair can bypass.

Usage: `const guardedTools = sdk.toolAdapter(tools);`

sections.heading: Adapt an API client
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.clientAdapter<T extends object>(target: T, options?: ClientOptions): T`

Parameters: A supported client object. ClientOptions.tool accepts a string or dynamic function. Authentication, connection and storage methods are excluded from HTTP interception.

Returns: A wrapped target of type T with supported method receivers preserved.

Failures: Unsupported or immutable methods can be unchanged. Runtime call failures follow guard; no complete framework batch/stream guarantee.

Usage: `const guardedClient = sdk.clientAdapter(client);`

sections.heading: Adapt HTTP
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.httpAdapter<T extends object>(target: T, options?: GuardOptions): T`

Parameters: A supported fetch/HTTP/Express shape and optional tool/operation policy. Supported request/response projections are adapter-specific.

Returns: An HTTP-shaped target of type T. A returned Response stays a Response.

Failures: Incomplete, opaque or streaming bodies can bypass inspection rather than inventing evidence. Unsupported forms do not gain automatic repair.

Usage: `const guardedFetch = sdk.httpAdapter(fetch, { tool: 'orders.get' });`

sections.heading: Update future-call policy
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.configure(config: Config): void`

Parameters: config contains call policy, not construction-only selection, work or selectiveRepair. Later revisions affect future calls, including previously created guards.

Returns: void; an executing call retains its frozen configuration.

Failures: Invalid explicit configuration throws AgindowSetupError. Semantic-write protections and strict policy cannot be disabled by failClosed opt-out.

Usage: `sdk.configure({ mode: 'observe' });`

sections.heading: Subscribe to events
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.on(kind: Event['type'], listener: (event: Event) => void): () => void`

Parameters: kind is drift, repair, blocked, bypass or error; listener receives bounded frozen metadata.

Returns: An unsubscribe function. No success event is emitted solely for completing a call.

Failures: Listener faults are contained. Events are not durable storage and cannot change the engine decision.

Usage: `const stop = sdk.on('bypass', event => console.warn(event.tool)); stop();`

sections.heading: Read recent events
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.recent(): readonly Event[]`

Parameters: No parameters. buffer defaults to 100; 0 disables retention.

Returns: A bounded history in emission order. Empty history does not prove detection was selected, eligible or drift-free.

Failures: Missing optional audit/feedback metadata remains absent; history is process-local and not a durable archive.

Usage: `const events = sdk.recent();`

sections.heading: Simulate a recording
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.simulate(tool: string, input: SimulationInput): Simulation`

Parameters: input requires recorded, with optional args, partial, contract and guard policy. No provider request is made.

Returns: status (no_drift/observed/blocked/bypassed/repaired/degraded), driftClass, confidence, changes, byte_identical and wouldWrite. A supplied sandbox contract is a distinct evaluation path.

Failures: Partial evidence and internal failures return bypassed; invalid setup can throw AgindowSetupError. Simulation does not establish real vendor acceptance.

Usage: `const result = sdk.simulate('orders.get', { recorded: savedOrder, operation: 'read' });`

sections.heading: Drain the optional audit FIFO
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.drainAudit(sink: AuditSink, limit?: number): Promise<AuditDrain>`

Parameters: sink persists a detached AuditRecord after the guarded call. limit defaults to 64. Construction requires explicit audit options; cannot be combined with selectiveRepair.

Returns: A Promise with delivered, pending, dropped and available. Acknowledge only after persistence succeeds.

Failures: Unavailable guest/drain or sink failure stays visible through the receipt; no durable replay guarantee is supplied.

Usage: `const receipt = await sdk.drainAudit(persistAudit);`

sections.heading: Execute through an explicit remote host
sections.text:
Signature: `guardRemote<T>(original: (input: RemoteEnvelope) => T | Promise<T>, envelope: RemoteEnvelope, options: RemoteOptions): Promise<Response | T>`

Parameters: original is your fallback, envelope describes the scoped call, and options requires endpoint with optional timeoutMs (5000), apiKey or auth, onEvent and onAuthDiagnostic. Writes/unknown require idempotency_key.

Returns: A fetch Response or original fallback result T. Read the response body once.

Failures: Setup misuse can throw AgindowSetupError; valid policy feedback throws AgindowDriftError. Unavailable transport/auth can fallback; completed vendor outcomes are not blindly replayed. No hosted endpoint is provided.

Usage: `const response = await guardRemote(fallback, envelope, options);`

sections.heading: Create remote authentication
sections.text:
Signature: `createRemoteAuth(options: RemoteAuthOptions): Promise<RemoteAuth>`

Parameters: options.acquire(thumbprint) returns Promise<AccessCredential> with accessToken and Unix-seconds expiresAt. Optional signer, now, schedule, allowLegacyFallback, legacyKey and onDiagnostic control local lifecycle.

Returns: A session with headers(method, target), refresh(): Promise<boolean>, close(): void. Header generation reads memory/signs locally; acquisition/refresh is off-path.

Failures: Unavailable initial identity without an explicitly accepted legacy fallback throws AgindowSetupError. headers may return undefined and refresh may return false. Close stops timers and clears cached credentials.

Usage: `const auth = await createRemoteAuth({ acquire });`

sections.heading: Create a proof signer
sections.text:
Signature: `createProofSigner(): ProofSigner`

Parameters: No parameters. Creates an ephemeral Ed25519 keypair inside this process.

Returns: thumbprint and proof(token, method, target, now): string; now is Unix seconds. No private-key serialization is exposed.

Failures: Invalid HTTP proof targets can throw AgindowSetupError. A response-provided key does not establish trust.

Usage: `const signer = createProofSigner();`

sections.heading: Prepare workload acquisition
sections.text:
Signature: `workloadIdentity(options: WorkloadIdentityOptions): (thumbprint: string) => Promise<AccessCredential>`

Parameters: Required exchangeEndpoint, registration and tools. Optional audience, ttl, tokenFile or assertion callback. Registration grants scope, not a local tenant string.

Returns: An acquire callback for createRemoteAuth. Assertion/file/provider I/O runs only during setup/background refresh.

Failures: Invalid endpoint throws AgindowSetupError; unavailable assertion or failed exchange rejects acquisition. No machine registration is automatically provisioned.

Usage: `const acquire = workloadIdentity(identityOptions);`

sections.heading: Default exports and public types
sections.text: agindow is the default SDK instance. Module-level guard, wrap, toolAdapter, clientAdapter, httpAdapter and simulate delegate to it. There is no module-level configure/on/recent export and no embedded sdk.close method. Use the instance for configuration and event lifecycle.

rows: Mode, Operation, Callable, Config (AgindowConfig alias), Options, GuardOptions, StatisticalSelection, Transformer; complete fields in configuration.
Event (AgindowEvent alias), Verdict, PolicyFeedback, VerifiedRepair; fields in events/verdicts reference.
SelectiveRepairOptions, RenameRule, RepairCheck; confidence, scope and synchronous verification rules in configuration.
ToolLike, ToolMap, ToolArray, ClientOptions, SimulationInput, Simulation, SandboxContract, SandboxFields, SandboxResult. Sandbox types describe explicit offline contracts, not runtime discovery.
AuditSink, AuditRecord, AuditDrain, Engine, EngineCall, EngineLoader. Host/test seams do not enable an external engine service.
RemoteEnvelope, RemoteOptions, RemoteAuth, RemoteAuthOptions, AccessCredential, ProofSigner, WorkloadIdentityOptions.
AgindowSetupError and AgindowDriftError: phase, verdict, outcome, code, hint, driftClass, driftId and auditUrl. Optional/missing evidence is not a link guarantee.

sections.heading: Types and conventions
sections.text: Import public names from agindow. P/R below stand for the original callable ParamSpec and return type. Config and event names are Python-specific; ready is a synchronous property. The practical guide covers decorators and async calls first.

sections.heading: Construct an instance
sections.text:
Signature: `Agindow(config: Config | None = None, *, engine: Engine | None = None, selection: dict[str, object] | None = None, selective_repair: SelectiveRepair | None = None, work: int = 200_000_000, **overrides: object)`

Parameters: config supplies an optional Config object. Keyword overrides supply Python call settings. selection/work/selective_repair are construction-only. engine is an advanced host/test seam and cannot be combined with selective repair.

Returns: An Agindow instance; construction attempts the engine load synchronously. An explicit Config object replaces resolved configuration as documented.

Failures: Invalid configuration raises AgindowSetupError. Engine load exceptions are retained in load_error; later guarded calls bypass.

Usage: `sdk = Agindow(mode="observe")`

sections.heading: Inspect readiness
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.ready: bool; sdk.load_error: Exception | None`

Parameters: No parameters. Read the properties after construction.

Returns: ready indicates that an engine exists, while load_error retains its load failure. Neither establishes that a detector is selected.

Failures: Never await sdk.ready. A failed load preserves original calls via bypass rather than an SDK-generated request exception.

Usage: `if not sdk.ready: print("Inspection unavailable")`

sections.heading: Decorate or guard a callable
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.guard(fn=None, *, tool: str | None = None, operation: Operation = "read", **changes: object)`

Parameters: fn is Callable[P, R]; omitted fn returns a decorator. tool names the operation; operation labels read/write/unknown, while changes supplies call policy.

Returns: Callable[P, R] or a decorator producing it. Sync functions stay sync; coroutine functions stay async. Arguments, results and exceptions retain the original behavior in observe mode.

Failures: Invalid setup raises AgindowSetupError. Original exceptions/cancellation propagate. Policy can raise AgindowDriftError; response-phase outcome may already be completed.

Usage: `@sdk.guard(tool="orders.get", operation="read")`

sections.heading: Wrap a callable directly
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.wrap(target: Callable[P, R], *, tool: str | None = None, operation: Operation = "read", **changes: object) -> Callable[P, R]`

Parameters: target is one callable, not a Node-style tool collection/client/HTTP adapter.

Returns: A guarded callable with the same sync/async contract.

Failures: Same setup, policy, upstream and availability semantics as guard; no automatic Python framework selection.

Usage: `read = sdk.wrap(client.get_order, tool="orders.get")`

sections.heading: Apply task-local scopes
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.context(**options: object) -> Scope`

Parameters: Python call-policy overrides for this SDK instance. Scope supports __enter__/__exit__ and __aenter__/__aexit__.

Returns: A synchronous/asynchronous context manager. It applies ContextVar overrides and restores the previous scope on exit. Executing calls retain a frozen snapshot.

Failures: Invalid options or re-entering the same active scope raises AgindowSetupError. Context exit does not swallow application exceptions or cancellation.

Usage: `async with sdk.context(mode="observe"): await read_order()`

sections.heading: Update future calls
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.configure(**changes: object) -> None`

Parameters: Python call-policy fields; construction-only engine selection is separate. Decorator keyword overrides can take precedence over instance/context settings.

Returns: None; future calls use the updated policy and resized event buffer.

Failures: Invalid changes raise AgindowSetupError. Do not assume Node revision precedence is identical.

Usage: `sdk.configure(mode="observe", buffer=100)`

sections.heading: Subscribe to local events
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.on(kind: EventType, listener: Callable[[Event], None]) -> Callable[[], None]`

Parameters: kind is drift, repair, blocked, bypass or error. EventType describes those literals; use an event kind string at the public call boundary.

Returns: An unsubscribe callable. Listeners receive Event metadata with snake_case fields.

Failures: Listener exceptions are contained. A callback cannot authorize a repair or establish persistence.

Usage: `stop = sdk.on("bypass", lambda event: print(event.tool)); stop()`

sections.heading: Read local events
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.recent() -> tuple[Event, ...]`

Parameters: No parameters. Config.buffer defaults to 100; 0 disables retention.

Returns: A bounded event tuple. No normal-success event is emitted. Empty history does not establish detector eligibility or safety.

Failures: Local history is not durable storage and does not imply an audit artifact was retained.

Usage: `events = sdk.recent()`

sections.heading: Close the engine
sections.text:
Signature: `sdk.close() -> None`

Parameters: No parameters. Use a finally block when your instance owns a finite operation lifecycle.

Returns: None. Releases the engine and contains cleanup faults; subsequent guarded calls bypass.

Failures: Cleanup failure must not replace upstream outcomes. Closing an instance is distinct from cancelling a vendor operation.

Usage: `sdk.close()`

sections.heading: Configure reviewed repair
sections.text:
Signature: `SelectiveRepair(rules: tuple[RenameRule, ...], verify: Callable[[RepairCheck], bool])`

Parameters: RenameRule(tool, side, source, target, migration, confidence) scopes reviewed top-level fields. RepairCheck(before: str, after: str, rule: RenameRule) supplies immutable JSON to a synchronous independent verifier.

Returns: A construction option passed as selective_repair. Acceptance requires reviewed facts, complete capture, confidence and repair/strict mode.

Failures: Invalid rules raise AgindowSetupError. Verifier faults or async results bypass. A false verifier does not authorize application; existing findings are not cleared to force repair.

Usage: `sdk = Agindow(selective_repair=reviewed_repair, mode="observe")`

sections.heading: Use the module-level instance
sections.text:
Signature: `default() -> Agindow`

Parameters: No parameters. Lazily constructs one module-owned instance.

Returns: Module-level guard, wrap, context, configure and recent delegate to that instance. Their callable/return contracts match the instance methods.

Failures: No module-level on or close helper is exported; call default().on(...) or default().close() explicitly. Prefer independent instances for application-owned lifecycles.

Usage: `from agindow import guard, context, configure, recent`

sections.heading: Call a remote host synchronously
sections.text:
Signature: `guard_remote(original: Callable[[RemoteEnvelope], R], envelope: RemoteEnvelope, options: RemoteOptions) -> RemoteResponse | R`

Parameters: original supplies fallback. RemoteEnvelope(tool, connection, operation, args, mode, idempotency_key=None); RemoteOptions(endpoint, api_key=None, timeout_seconds=5, on_event=None, auth=None, on_auth_diagnostic=None).

Returns: RemoteResponse(status, headers, body) or fallback R. response.read(amount=None) returns bytes; response.close() releases its transport.

Failures: Setup misuse raises AgindowSetupError; valid policy feedback raises AgindowDriftError. Transport/auth failure can fallback. A completed vendor outcome is not blindly replayed; writes/unknown need the same vendor-enforced idempotency key.

Usage: `response = guard_remote(fallback, envelope, options)`

sections.heading: Call a remote host asynchronously
sections.text:
Signature: `async guard_remote_async(original: Callable[[RemoteEnvelope], R], envelope: RemoteEnvelope, options: RemoteOptions) -> RemoteResponse | R`

Parameters: Same envelope/options and synchronous fallback contract as guard_remote. The blocking transport executes in a worker thread.

Returns: Awaitable yielding RemoteResponse or R; close remote responses after reading.

Failures: Same setup, policy and fallback rules. Cancelling the await does not prove a worker/vendor write stopped.

Usage: `response = await guard_remote_async(fallback, envelope, options)`

sections.heading: Sign proofs and refresh remote identity
sections.text:
Signature: `RemoteAuth(acquire, signer, *, now=time, schedule=True, allow_legacy_fallback=False, legacy_key=None, on_diagnostic=None)`

Parameters: acquire: Callable[[str], AccessCredential]; AccessCredential(access_token: str, expires_at: int). ProofSigner(public_x: str, sign: Callable[[bytes], bytes]) keeps host-owned Ed25519 custody.

Returns: RemoteAuth.headers(method, target) -> dict[str, str] | None; refresh() -> bool; close() -> None. ProofSigner.thumbprint and proof(token, method, target, now) -> str. Acquisition runs at setup/background refresh, not guarded calls.

Failures: Initial unavailable identity without explicit fallback raises AgindowSetupError. Failed refresh returns false and unavailable headers return None. Invalid public keys/targets refuse. Close stops timers and releases cached credentials.

Usage: `auth = RemoteAuth(acquire, signer)`

sections.heading: Prepare workload acquisition
sections.text:
Signature: `workload_identity(*, exchange_endpoint, registration, tools, audience="agindow:guard", ttl=300, token_file=None, assertion=None) -> Callable[[str], AccessCredential]`

Parameters: exchange_endpoint and registration are strings; tools is tuple[str, ...]. Optional token_file: str and assertion: Callable[[], str] supply host-owned workload material.

Returns: An acquire callback for RemoteAuth; registration fixes authority. No tenant argument grants scope.

Failures: Invalid endpoint raises AgindowSetupError; missing assertions and failed exchanges fail acquisition. Provider I/O occurs outside guarded calls, with no automatic registration.

Usage: `acquire = workload_identity(exchange_endpoint=url, registration=registration, tools=tools)`

sections.heading: Configuration, models and exceptions
sections.text: Config is a frozen dataclass with mode, fail_closed, api_key, endpoint, allowed_tools, deny_tools, buffer and on_event. Mode and Operation are literal type aliases. Event, Verdict, PolicyFeedback and VerifiedRepair are frozen data models; Python Verdict does not expose Node detector-name arrays. AgindowSetupError identifies deterministic ValueError setup misuse. AgindowDriftError is a RuntimeError exposing tool, mode, phase, verdict, outcome, code, hint, drift_class, drift_id and audit_url. The Python root exports Agindow, Scope, Config, Event, Mode, Operation, PolicyFeedback, Verdict, VerifiedRepair, the two error classes, RenameRule, RepairCheck, SelectiveRepair, remote models/functions, RemoteAuth, AccessCredential, ProofSigner and workload_identity, plus default/guard/wrap/context/configure/recent. It exports no Node adapters, simulation method, CLI or guest audit drain.

sections.heading: Configuration overview
sections.text: Control how AGINDOW observes integration behavior, detects supported drift and applies eligible verified repairs. Make three choices: which tool operations to inspect, which scoped evidence to compare, and how to handle eligible drift. Start in observe. Construction settings load the engine, detector selection and repair rules. Per-operation settings name the tool, label read/write/unknown and choose call policy. Readiness alone does not activate detection.

sections.heading: Minimal configuration
sections.text: Runnable setup fixtures: use Node 22.6+ for the native TypeScript command. Install the selected SDK, save the tab as config.mts or config.py and run node --experimental-strip-types config.mts or python config.py. The embedded SDK needs no AGINDOW key or endpoint. All shown options are optional construction values; mode defaults to observe, allowed tools to all and event buffer to 100. The explicit tool/operation describes this callable. Node readiness is a settling Promise; Python readiness is a boolean and load_error retains failure. An unavailable engine bypasses. This example preserves a local read, but meaningful statistical findings require the selection below.

sections.heading: Configure SDK modes
sections.text: Use observe for initial integration. Enable repair only after reviewing rules and evaluating independent verification. Strict applies the configured halt policy when eligible evidence cannot be resolved; it cannot prevent an already completed upstream operation or make unavailable inspection safe. Infrastructure faults still bypass in every mode.

rows: Inspect and report selected evidence. Never mutates or policy-blocks the original operation.
Apply supported verified repairs at confidence ≥0.97. Unresolved reads degrade and shape drift passes through; semantic writes block. Unknown writes default closed.
Apply verified repairs at confidence ≥0.99. Matched unresolved drift halts under strict policy, including incomplete repair; failClosed opt-out is ignored.

sections.heading: Configure drift detection
sections.text: Runnable labelled magnitude-shift fixture: save as detect-config.mts or detect_config.py and use the same runtime commands as above. StatisticalSelection scopes tenant, connection, vendor, operation and segment; operation must match the guarded tool name. fields selects a JSON Pointer and request/response phase; baseline and live contain complete raw JSON documents from comparable independent calls. Production windows must come from permitted representative observations, not copies of one call. This small synthetic exercise supplies 128 samples per window and expects a drift event with the original value retained. Eligibility is detector-specific, not a universal 128-sample promise. Too few samples, missing fields, incompatible evidence or exhausted work can make detection ineligible or unavailable; no findings is not proof of a clean integration. Optional materiality sets a floor in (0,1], not repair permission. Keep selection outside configure updates.

sections.heading: Enable selective repair
sections.text: Selective repair is off by default. Supply reviewed top-level rename facts through Node selectiveRepair: {rules, verify}, or Python selective_repair=SelectiveRepair(rules=(RenameRule(...),), verify=verify). The independent synchronous verifier receives immutable RepairCheck before/after JSON and the scoped rule; exactly true/True accepts. The runnable local example below checks a reviewed customer-name snapshot, first observes unchanged input, then applies contact_name → display_name in repair mode and checks a repair event. Run it as repair.mts or repair.py. Replace the fixture data/callable with your reviewed application facts and existing client; prepare authoritative facts off-path, without verifier network/database/LLM calls. It is not arbitrary semantic correction, source rewriting or PR publication.

sections.heading: Configuration recipes
sections.text:
A — Observe an existing integration: use the minimal configuration and replace the local callable with your existing API client; name the tool and operation.
B — Detect a supported field change: add a scoped selection with comparable representative windows; inspect drift events and eligibility, as in the compact detection fixture.
C — Enable a reviewed repair: provide reviewed rename rules and independent verifier at construction, observe first, then configure repair after evaluation. Inspect repair events; mere proposals are not applied repairs.
D — Control failure behavior: failClosed defaults true. Setting false affects unknown writes in repair mode; it does not opt semantic writes out, and strict ignores the opt-out. Reads in repair degrade rather than block. Internal faults bypass, while upstream exceptions propagate. Request policy halts precede dispatch; response halts retain an already completed outcome. Inspect AgindowDriftError.phase and outcome before any retry. These are configuration recipes; the earlier complete programs are local executable fixtures, not live vendor qualification.

sections.heading: Repair rule reference
sections.text: Node RenameRule uses tool, side, from, to, migration and confidence. Python RenameRule uses tool, side, source, target, migration and confidence. Keys are simple top-level object names of up to 64 ASCII letters, digits or underscores, starting with a letter or underscore. One rule per tool/side, at most 16 rules. Tool and migration IDs contain 1–256 non-control characters. confidence is a required finite number from 0 to 1; side is request or response. All rule fields are required. The verifier receives RepairCheck with before, after and rule, returning exactly true/True to approve. It must check independent authoritative meaning or business evidence; copying values or validating a schema alone cannot establish intent. Prepare evidence outside calls; do not perform network or database I/O in the verifier.

sections.heading: Repair decisions and limits
sections.text: Observe reports matched rules without changing payloads. Repair requires confidence at least 0.97; strict requires 0.99. Source absence preserves identity. Destination collisions, low confidence and verifier refusal leave payloads unchanged; strict halts matched unresolved drift, and repair passes unresolved shape drift through under the shared Rust policy; semantic-write blocks remain in force. Statistical findings or halts, malformed results and bypass are never cleared to permit a repair. Verifier faults, async results and unavailable capture preserve upstream behavior through bypass. Supported payloads are plain JSON objects and Node RawJson boundaries, with complete captures up to 1 MiB. Opt-in repair divides the work allowance across statistical inspection and the two preparation phases. Numeric/unit/enum rewrites, nested/array migrations and automatic discovery are outside this option. Node guest audit FIFO cannot be combined with selectiveRepair; use repair events for local observation. This does not provide a durable repair archive or persisted write proof.

sections.text: Both Event types expose type, tool, mode, phase and optional verdict. Node uses latencyUs, driftClass, auditId and byte_identical, with optional reason and side. Python uses latency_us, drift_class, audit_id and byte_identical. Latency is diagnostic timing, not an SLA. Optional evidence may be absent; do not invent an artifact URL or treat it as successful retention.

sections.heading: Verdict reference
sections.text: Verdict contains halt, bypassed, findings, detectors and malformed. Node class corresponds to Python drift_class. Optional confidence, feedback and repair describe engine evidence. Local event callbacks omit the replacement repair body; use the returned payload and repair event to observe an applied change. Node exposes eligibleDetectors, suppressedDetectors and detectorKinds when supplied; the Python Verdict does not expose those detector arrays. A detector count is not a finding count, and a zero finding count does not establish that inspection was eligible or configured.

sections.heading: Errors preserve phase and outcome
sections.text: AgindowSetupError identifies deterministic misuse before execution. AgindowDriftError exposes tool, mode, phase, verdict and outcome for policy halts. Node also exposes code, hint, driftClass, driftId and auditUrl; Python uses drift_class, drift_id and audit_url. Original upstream failures propagate; policy wrapping retains a cause where available. Inspect a completed response outcome before considering another write.
